FindingIdDto.description: A report finding ID: `F-` and the finding's number, written with at least two digits and no other leading zero, such as `F-01` or `F-100`.

NoteSection.description: A section of the report, which `save_section` writes.

PageCursorDto.description: An opaque keyset continuation for list resources.

read_draft.description: Reads the saved findings and sections. With no field it returns the short list. Give `ids` or `sections`, not both.

cursor.description: The cursor a previous result returned. Send it with the same `ids` or `sections`.

ids.description: Findings to read in full. Leave out `sections` when you give these.

sections.description: Sections to read in full. `extra` reads every extra section. Leave out `ids` when you give these.

read_draft.title: ReadDraft

FindingBasis.description: What the agent confirmed (`observed`) or could not verify (`gap`).

FindingIdDto.description: A report finding ID: `F-` and the finding's number, written with at least two digits and no other leading zero, such as `F-01` or `F-100`.

FindingLocation.description: A file a finding points at, with an optional 1-based line.

Severity.description: A finding's severity, most severe first.

save_finding.description: Saves a new finding, or changes the finding named by `id`. A new finding gives `title`, `severity`, `blocking`, `kind`, `issue`, `consequence` and `evidence`. A change gives `id`, `expectedRevision` and only the fields it changes.

blocking.description: Whether the lead holds the merge on this finding.

category.description: A one-line label without `·`, such as Security or Tests. Defaults to the kind's name.

consequence.description: Markdown starting with a paragraph: why it matters.

details.description: Markdown for diagrams, tables and longer reasoning, shown after the evidence. An empty string removes it.

expectedRevision.description: The revision you last read of the finding named by `id`. Required with `id`.

id.description: The finding to change. Leave it out to save a new finding.

issue.description: Markdown starting with a paragraph: what is wrong.

kind.description: `functional` or `quality`. Security and correctness concerns are functional.

locations.description: The files the finding points at. An empty list removes them.

proposedComment.description: Markdown starting with a paragraph: the comment the lead would post. An empty string removes it.

title.description: One line naming the problem, without a severity label such as `P1 –`.

save_finding.title: SaveFinding

NoteSection.description: A section of the report, which `save_section` writes.

save_section.description: Replaces one section of the report.

body.description: The section's Markdown. An empty body removes the section, except a required one.

expectedRevision.description: The revision you last read of this section. Required once the section exists.

section.description: `title` is the report's title, on one line. `summary` says what the MR does in at most four plain paragraphs and `rationale` gives the reason for the verdict in one. `flow` is a Mermaid diagram of the principal code and data flow in a fenced block that opens with a line ```mermaid, then a short explanation. `changes` is a table with the two columns Before and After, then a table with the columns Affected operation, What changes and Source. `threads`, `questions`, `verification` and `publication` fill the report sections of those names, and `extra` adds a section under its own title. A first version or a full review needs `summary`, `rationale`, `flow`, `changes` and `verification`, and once saved they cannot be removed.

title.description: One line naming an `extra` section. Required for `extra` and only for it.

save_section.title: SaveSection

DiscussionIdDto.description: A GitLab discussion ID of a selected-thread batch.

FindingIdDto.description: A report finding ID: `F-` and the finding's number, written with at least two digits and no other leading zero, such as `F-01` or `F-100`.

GitShaDto.description: A full SHA-1 or SHA-256 Git object name.

set_finding_outcome.description: Sets what became of a finding already saved.

checkedSha.description: The commit you checked, when it differs from the revision you give to submit_review.

discussionIds.description: The GitLab discussions this outcome answers.

expectedRevision.description: The revision you last read of this finding.

outcome.description: `fixed`, `clarified_withdrawn` and `superseded` retire the finding. The others keep it active.

reason.description: One line saying what you checked.

set_finding_outcome.title: SetFindingOutcome

Assessment.description: The lead's conclusion on one selected discussion of a follow-up batch.

DiscussionIdDto.description: A GitLab discussion ID of a selected-thread batch.

FindingIdDto.description: A report finding ID: `F-` and the finding's number, written with at least two digits and no other leading zero, such as `F-01` or `F-100`.

ReportRevision.description: The reviewed revision: `{sha}` with the exact full SHA, or `{sha: null, reason}` when it is unknown.

reason.description: Why the reviewed commit is unknown. Only with a null sha.

sha.description: The full SHA of the reviewed commit, or null when it is unknown.

submit_review.description: Closes the review and publishes a version. A first or full review needs `verdict`, `revision` and the `summary`, `rationale`, `flow`, `changes` and `verification` sections; a selected-thread check needs one entry in `assessments` per selected discussion.

assessments.description: One per selected discussion of a selected-thread check, and only there.

fullReview.description: Publish a full review of the whole MR. Every active finding of the last version must then be changed or given an outcome.

revision.description: The reviewed commit. Required for a first version and a full review. ReviewQ binds a selected-thread check's commit itself.

verdict.description: Required for a first version and a full review. Otherwise it defaults to the current version's verdict.

submit_review.title: SubmitReview

wait_for_user.description: Pauses the review until the user replies to a question that must be answered before the review can finish. It publishes nothing.

question.description: The question, and what the review waits on. Ask it in your reply as well: the user is told only that the review needs input.

wait_for_user.title: WaitForUser
